tagline.text: A butterfly garden and Palaw'an village, a city-tour staple

location.label: Location
location.text: Sta. Monica area, Puerto Princesa City, along the South Road

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱50–700 (entrance plus tricycle city tour, per person)

children.text: This small butterfly garden lies in the Sta. Monica area, a short way south of Puerto Princesa's center. You watch butterflies inside a netted garden, then see fire-making and blowpipe demonstrations at a Palaw'an indigenous village, a regular stop on city tours.

The Palawan Butterfly Ecological Garden and Tribal Village is a small eco-garden in the Sta. Monica area, a little south of Puerto Princesa's center. As the name says, it offers two things in one place. One is a butterfly garden where butterflies fly under a net roof, and the other is a village where the Palaw'an, an indigenous people of Palawan island, show their traditional way of life. OpenStreetMap and map services place it along the Puerto Princesa South Road at about 9.795, 118.732.

It is not big. One travel information site says a visit takes 45–60 minutes, while another says about 30 minutes. That is why most people stop here as one part of a Puerto Princesa city tour rather than as a destination of its own. Many travelers combine it with Mitra's Ranch and Baker's Hill, which lie in the same direction, for a half-day route. Unlike a full-day plan such as the Underground River tour or Honda Bay island hopping, it fits well into a rainy day or the spare hours on an arrival or departure day.

Besides butterflies, there is an area showing insects and small animals such as scorpions, giant millipedes and stick insects, and travel blogs mention crocodiles, wild pigs and boa constrictors. A guide walks beside you and explains, so families with children tend to enjoy it. Some reviews say the number of butterfly species is smaller than expected, so you will be happier if you treat it as a light stop rather than expecting a large butterfly farm.

The tribal village is what makes this place special, and also what divides opinion. Palaw'an people show fire-making, blowpipe demonstrations and music in front of a model of a traditional house, and visitors support the village with a small tip or by buying handicrafts on top of the entrance fee. Some visitors call it a genuine cultural exchange, while others felt uneasy about being spectators. It is good manners to ask before taking photos and to say thanks with a tip or a souvenir after the demonstration.

The space where butterflies fly is enclosed by netting so you can see them up close. They are most active in the morning, so visit right after opening or earlier in the day. Do not use a flash, since it startles the butterflies, and if one lands on your hand or shoulder, wait patiently instead of shaking it off.

There is an area showing insects and small animals such as scorpions, giant millipedes and stick insects. According to one travel blog, a staff member explained that scorpions do not sting unless provoked. If you bring children, listen to the staff and do not let them touch the animals.

In front of a model of a traditional house, Palaw'an people show fire-making, blowpipe demonstrations and instrument playing. You can hear about hunting and daily life, which makes this a short introduction to the culture of the Philippines' indigenous peoples. Demonstration times can vary from day to day, so ask when you arrive.

There is a spot selling handicrafts made by villagers and butterfly-themed souvenirs. One travel blog describes buying village handicrafts as a direct way to help the residents. Prices are often not fixed, so bring small bills and ask politely.

Reviews mention island animals such as the Palawan peacock and the Palawan bearcat. However, the animals may be hiding and you may not see them on some days (one blog says the peacock was not seen), so do not count on seeing them.

blocks.title: Starting point of a city-tour combo

children.text: The view from Mitra's Ranch and the bread and theme garden of Baker's Hill lie in the same direction, so they combine easily. One blog described a half-day route that went from the Butterfly Garden to Mitra's Ranch and stopped at Baker's Hill on the way back.

items.title: One-hour route (stand-alone visit)
items.subtitle: See the garden and village, then move on

children.text: Arrive around opening time and buy a ticket. Butterflies are most active just after opening and there are fewer visitors.
Walk slowly through the butterfly garden. A guide often walks beside you, so feel free to ask questions.
Look around the insect and animal exhibits. If you are with children, look only and follow the staff's instructions.
Watch the demonstration at the tribal village and thank the performers at the end with a tip or a handicraft purchase.
Move on to your next stop by tricycle or Grab.
Opening hours (reported as 8:30 AM–5:00 PM) may change on public holidays and other days, so check before you go.

items.title: Half-day city-tour route
items.subtitle: Butterfly garden · Mitra's Ranch · Baker's Hill

children.text: Hire a tricycle from your accommodation and set off. City-tour drivers usually know the order of this route.
Spend about 1 hour at the Palawan Butterfly Garden.
Move on to Mitra's Ranch for the city view. According to one blog, the ranch grounds were free and the museum had a separate fee.
At Baker's Hill, buy bread and snacks and look around the theme garden.
Return to the city center for lunch.
It helps to agree on the route order and waiting time with the driver beforehand.
A nonstop flight from Manila (NAIA) to Puerto Princesa International Airport (PPS) takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change often, so check when you book.
There are also nonstop flights into PPS from other cities such as Cebu; check airline announcements.

items.title: From the airport or city center to the garden

children.text: A tricycle is the most common choice. One travel blog said a tricycle going straight to the garden cost about
(negotiable), and another said the road leg during a city tour took about
30 minutes
. It varies with where you start.
A taxi or Grab is easy to call from a hotel in the city. Tell the driver the English name and the area together, such as "Butterfly Garden, Sta. Monica".
There is a note that regular public transport does not connect directly to the garden, so decide on your transport in advance.
It may be hard to find a taxi on the way back, so first check whether you can hire a round trip or call a Grab.
If you book a Puerto Princesa city tour at your accommodation or a travel agency, the Butterfly Garden is usually included. According to one blog, city-tour packages cost about
per person depending on the number of stops, and another report said a half-day tricycle hire cost
for up to four people.
A van hire for 4 hours was recorded at about
. These are all past reports, so check current prices yourself.

Mornings are best. Butterflies are most active in the morning before the temperature rises, and there are fewer visitors. There are reports that indigenous demonstrations are often held in the afternoon, so afternoons are not bad if the demonstrations matter most to you.

For the season, the dry months of November–May are the most comfortable for walking. In the rainy season you can still tour the sections under the net roof, but butterflies are less active on rainy days. One blog said photos were taken even on a drizzly day.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Good butterfly activity and peak season for city tours. A morning visit is recommended.
Go right after opening to avoid the midday heat.
Showers are common. Bring an umbrella and pair it with indoor stops.

items.label: Entrance fee
items.note: Most blogs say ₱50; a 2026 information site and a review say ₱60. There are reports of student and senior discounts, but this needs confirming

items.label: Guide tip
items.note: A thank-you for the guide's explanation and the indigenous demonstrations

items.label: Handicrafts
items.note: Made by villagers; prices vary by item

items.note: Up to 4 people, per one blog (past report)

Food inside the garden is limited to small stalls, so people usually eat in the city or at the next stop. One information site mentions Kinabuch Grill & Bar and Kalui Restaurant as nearby restaurants. There are not many restaurants around the garden, so it is easier to return to the city for lunch.
Most people stay in the city center of Puerto Princesa rather than near the garden and travel from there. For information on the city, see the Puerto Princesa City entry.
Go early in the morning, when butterflies are active and there are few people. Indigenous demonstrations tend to be held in the afternoon.
Bring small bills (₱20, ₱50, ₱100). They are used for tips and handicraft purchases.
Do not use a flash on the butterflies, and ask permission before flying a drone.
Bring light, cool clothes, comfortable shoes and mosquito repellent. The garden has plants and water, so there may be mosquitoes.
If you are on a city tour, it is easier to agree in advance that the driver will wait until you come back.
If you have a student ID, ask whether you can get a discount. A discount has not been confirmed.
If you go with children, have them follow staff instructions in the scorpion and insect area.
Map services list a contact phone number, +63 917 597 5544, and a Facebook page. Numbers can change, so contact them in advance if you are visiting as a group.
Entrance fees and opening hours differ by source and change often. Check the latest information locally or on an official page before you visit.
The tribal village is a cultural demonstration by people who really live there. Ask permission before taking photos and do not treat them rudely.
Do not touch or harass butterflies, insects or reptiles. Scorpions and snakes are especially dangerous.
Some reviews say that if your expectations are high, the small scale can disappoint. Think of it as one stop on a city tour.
Demonstration times and animal exhibits can vary from day to day. You may not see some animals.
It can be hard to call a taxi, so arrange your transport back in advance.
Reviews mention that the city center is about
30 minutes
away by tricycle. It is easy to continue to other city-tour stops.
An island-hopping route on the coast north of Puerto Princesa, best planned as a separate full-day trip.
The Underground River national park is far from the city and takes a full day. Plan the garden for a morning on a different day so the two do not overlap.
City-tour stops in the same direction as the Butterfly Garden. According to one blog, the Mitra's Ranch museum had a
fee and Baker's Hill had a

entrance fee in a 2020 report. Another guide also lists Mitra's Ranch at ₱20 per person, though this may vary by visit time and management policy, while a recent guide site says Baker's Hill has no entrance fee, so the reports conflict. Check on site.
